Data

The large files are served from a Butler University web directory, not from the Git repository. Each file is listed with its size and its SHA-256. The four byte-aligned cells are not hosted. Each one rebuilds from the oracle byte for byte, and its expected SHA-256 is listed below.

carmichael-1e24-cell001-n-classes.cnd

The sorted list of every Carmichael number n, split into residue classes modulo 10,810,800. Each class is stored by binary interpolative coding.

carmichael-1e24-cell101-dmin-classes.cnd

The sorted list of dmin(n), split into residue classes modulo 2310. Each class is stored by binary interpolative coding. Each n follows from dmin(n) once dmin(n) is factored.

carmichael-1e24-cell011-pwt-full.pwt2

A prime wavelet tree over the full prime factorization of every Carmichael number n, coded by rANS with context models. Every prime of every n is on its path, so no factoring is needed.

carmichael-1e24-cell111-pwt-dmin.pwt2

A prime wavelet tree over the primes of dmin(n) for every Carmichael number n, coded by rANS with context models. Decoding rebuilds each n from its path. The remaining primes of n come from factoring the cofactor r⋆.

carmichael-1e24-cell111x-pwt-dstar.pwt2

The tree of cell 111 over a different stopping divisor d∗(n) of each Carmichael number n. A heuristic search chooses d∗(n) to make the tree smaller, and it keeps dmin(n) for most numbers. Decoding works as for cell 111. The file stores the chosen divisors, so it can be rebuilt without repeating the search.

carmichael-1e24-oracle.orc1

The oracle is a lossless binary copy of the text table in which every prime factor is proven prime. It decodes to the text byte for byte. Certifying and rebuilding a cell need it.

Verifying a download

Check a file against SHA256SUMS with any of these commands. The repository holds the same SHA256SUMS. The make target also decodes the file.

curl -C - -O https://blue.butler.edu/~jewebste/prime-wavelet-tree/v1/carmichael-1e24-cell111x-pwt-dstar.pwt2
curl -O https://blue.butler.edu/~jewebste/prime-wavelet-tree/v1/SHA256SUMS
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS                                # Linux
shasum -a 256 carmichael-1e24-cell111x-pwt-dstar.pwt2                   # macOS
Get-FileHash carmichael-1e24-cell111x-pwt-dstar.pwt2 -Algorithm SHA256  # Windows PowerShell
make verify-111x                                                        # hash and decode

Licence and citation

The data files are public domain (CC0 1.0). They encode the table of A. Shallue and J. Webster. If you use them, please cite the table (Algorithms for Carmichael numbers, arXiv:2506.09903) and the paper (arXiv:2610.02550).

The source table

The original text table was computed by A. Shallue and J. Webster. It is served from its authors' web directory, which supports HTTP byte ranges. The oracle decodes to this file byte for byte.
